margin: not applicable - MultipleNegativesRankingLoss has no margin hyperparameter (unlike TripletMarginLoss). We chose MNRL specifically to avoid needing to tune this on a tiny dataset.
split_mode: fixed (default) or loto - both supported via --split-mode CLI flag
notes: Dataset is small: 144 fixed-split train triplets from only 6 unique anchor sentences. Kept epochs low (4) and batch size small (8) on purpose - more epochs on 6 anchors risks the model memorizing anchor-specific phrasing rather than learning a generalizable thesis-relevance signal, and a bigger batch size increases how often MNRL's in-batch-negative trick collides with duplicate positive texts (build_triplets.py generates a Cartesian product per thesis, so the same positive appears many times paired with different negatives). LOTO mode (8-fold leave-one-thesis-out, derived by combining train+val and holding out each thesis in turn) is the more trustworthy accuracy estimate given how tiny the fixed val split (2 theses) is. Validated with TripletEvaluator (% of triplets where positive scores more similar to anchor than negative) each epoch, keeping the best checkpoint rather than the final one.
